### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **43** documentable anchor(s).

**50** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json af2361ee85bf5e3d2192f9f69467bed67270f188`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 56 pages)`
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **67** of **249** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **48** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json af2361ee85bf5e3d2192f9f69467bed67270f188` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2a2015e717a66880688bb131e4bee10a86807f73` — the merge of head `6069a983f8f880e1a7f0b423abe2efe21fd258c8` into base `af2361ee85bf5e3d2192f9f69467bed67270f188`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2a2015e717a66880688bb131e4bee10a86807f73 && git checkout 2a2015e717a66880688bb131e4bee10a86807f73
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin af2361ee85bf5e3d2192f9f69467bed67270f188 6069a983f8f880e1a7f0b423abe2efe21fd258c8 && git checkout -B drift-repro af2361ee85bf5e3d2192f9f69467bed67270f188 && git merge --no-ff 6069a983f8f880e1a7f0b423abe2efe21fd258c8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json af2361ee85bf5e3d2192f9f69467bed67270f188
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs af2361ee85bf5e3d2192f9f69467bed67270f188` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

你定的两条评论权限，这个 PR 在服务端真正落实了，我读的部分没有发现问题：
① 能看到记录的人都能给任何一串评论点「已解决」，也能恢复；「已由 某某 解决」写的是点的人。新加的入口只改「已解决」这一项，评论文字照旧只有作者能改。
② 普通成员能删自己的评论，删不了别人的，能编辑记录也一样。自己的评论下面已经有回复的不能删（还可以改文字），这样就不会动到别人的回复。
平台原有的底线规则和权限设置一行没动，走原来的数据接口，结果和以前完全一样。开发环境里的实测结果（之前被拒的现在通过，该拒的照旧拒）都写在正文里。
另外提醒一点：这个 PR 合进去以后，手机评论页 #36208 有一条新测试的预期会变，那边合主干时要顺手改。
L1 结论：通过。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1-c) · repo:objectstack#1 · head `591de690` · 2026-11-22T00:31Z

**Card:** `Fixes #36186`, `Fixes #36191` (folded; seat claims 7069978538 / 7069989751). Rulings 7063285032 (option A) and 7069889899. Declarations: `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Not governed. 25 files, +1559 / −122.

**Gates:**
- CI is 63 success · 11 expected skip on `591de690`, and mergeable is clean.
- The branch is 12 behind `main`, and a trial merge is textually clean.
- `l1-face` FLAGGED two items, both accepted:
  - `Fixes #36191` is the fold.
  - `changeset` for `@objectstack/plugin-security` (`comment-doors.integration.test.ts`) and `@object-ui/plugin-form` (`affordanceGrantMap-12082.test.tsx`): both are test-only, so nothing ships.

### The doors against ruling 7069889899
- **Resolution door** (`comment-routes.ts`). The steps, in order:
  1. The caller, through the own-row doors' composition, with the 503 and API-key refusals.
  2. Anonymous: 401.
  3. A held sign-in: 403.
  4. Exactly `{ resolved: boolean }` with no query: anything else is 400.
  5. The comment read **as the caller**: object grant, organization wall and the comment read gate, so an unreadable comment and an unknown id are the same 404.
  6. A reply is 400, through the data door's own `refuseResolutionOnReply`.

  Then one system `update` of `{ is_resolved }` alone, by id, with `attributedUserId` set to the caller and the caller's tenant kept, and a read-back. Nothing but the one column is written, and nothing is written before every refusal is past.
  - This is the ruling's "dedicated resolve door": the floor is untouched, and there is no `sys_comment` update twin. The module doc states correctly why a twin is not possible (a row policy cannot scope a column).
  - External readers of the thread pass step 5, as the seat confirmed against option A's text.
- **`stampCommentResolution`.** The resolver is `session.userId ?? provenance.attributedUserId`, the audit writer's precedence. A session user still wins, and a system write with no attribution still stamps `null`. There is one side effect to know about, not a defect: any other system write that carries an attribution (a flow acting for a user) now names that user as `resolved_by` where it named `null`. That reads as the truer record.
- **Own-comment delete door.** It is the shared kit, with `ownerField: 'author_id'` (stamped and read-only), so another member's comment is 403 even for a record editor, and the moderator's delete stays the data door's.
  - The new step 7 of `OwnRowDeleteDoor`, `refuseRemoval`, runs after the owner check and before any removal. The other three doors declare none, so they are unchanged. `own-row-delete-routes.test.ts` gains 3 cases.
  - The comment door's step 7 is a system read of `parent_id = id`, giving 409 `DELETE_RESTRICTED`. It follows from the ruling (`parent_id` clears on delete, so the replies would become threads of their own), and the seat confirmed it as option B.
- **Routes.** There is no collision with the unreact door (`/comments/reactions/:id` has a different segment count). A `PUT /comments/reactions/resolution` would only read a comment id `reactions` and answer 404. The ledger rows are `gap`, with their conformance test, and `check-route-envelope` declares the module.
- **Proof on the real floor.** This is what #36104 lacked, and what my #36178 HOLD asked for.
  - `comment-doors.integration.test.ts` has 14 cases on a real kernel with `SecurityPlugin` and the shipped sets, SQLite, two plain `org_member` principals and an `org_admin`. Among them: a member's data-door `body`, `is_resolved`, and `{ is_resolved, body }` on a colleague's comment are all still 403. That is the ruling's required test.
  - The rig table repeats the HOLD readings before and after, with both members plain org members.

### The console against what the doors admit
- **✓** calls the resolution door on every resolvable root (`onResolveComment={feedsEnabled ? …}`), with no grant and no `updatesOthers` check. That matches the door: anyone who reads the record reads the thread. The row still changes only from the door's stored answer, and a refusal raises a toast and re-throws.
- **The explain probe** now gates only Edit on another person's comment, which is still floor-bound.
- **Delete:**
  - With the `sys_comment` delete grant, the data door, as before.
  - Without it, the delete goes to the door when `feedCommentDeleteOwn` allows it (`grant: 'create'`, the `feedReactionRemove` precedent), and the host sets `ownCommentDeletesOnly`. `deletableComment` then admits only the viewer's own comments with no reply. A reply counts if it is in `replyCount` or among the loaded replies, so a collapsed thread is covered too. The legacy `CommentBody` applies the same rule.
  - So the panel offers exactly the door's 200 rows. Everything the door answers 403 or 409 to has no control, short of a race.
  - A refused door delete is caught (`.catch` in `CommentThread`), so no unhandled rejection reaches the console.
- **Docs and changeset** (`plugin-detail.mdx`, `plugin-audit.md`, `36186-36191-comment-doors.md`): read sentence by sentence, and accurate apart from the nit below. The #36071 and #36075 notes stay byte-identical to `main`, and the new entry names the line each correction replaces, per the seat's 23:49Z rule.
- There is no Twenty-shaped code. The phone is #36208's, and nothing here touches the phone.

### Cross-PR, for the seat: #36208 after this lands
#36208 (approved at `e7d93e69`) lands after this PR. On the combined tree, its new `CommentsPage.test.tsx` case "the press engages before the hold opens…" asserts the sheet is `['delete']` before the verdict, for Grace's root `c2` (`resolved: false`, `onResolveComment` given).
- After this PR, `CommentThread` offers ✓ on every resolvable root whatever `updatesOthers` says, so that first reading becomes `['resolve', 'delete']`. The second reading (`['resolve', 'edit', 'delete']`) is unchanged.
- The trial merge of both onto `main` is textually clean, so the failure appears only when the tests run.
- #36208's thread should update that one expectation when it merges `main`. The app-shell case in that PR is unaffected, because its rows carry no `is_resolved`.

### Nit (does not block)
- The changeset says "A comment **others** replied to stays", and the docs say "someone has replied to". The door refuses any reply under the comment, the author's own included (`findOne({ parent_id })`), as the body's own table says ("own comment with a reply"). "A comment with any reply under it" would be exact.

L1 never replaces L2. The contract L2 (brief 7071567186) is the seat's.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `591de69037c4f208f98198bc09b270dcb1dd6e7b`
Local-runs: none

PR #36200 (cards #36186 and #36191), declaration face, tier raised by the seat because the PR adds two permission doors. Read: both cards with every comment, rulings 7069889899 and 7063285032, epic #36062, the bodies of #36104 and #36178, the PR body, its 25-path file list, the net diff against `main` (merge base `6c7c6db2`), and the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read to judge the doors, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

Judged against the rulings, door by door.

- **Resolution door, `PUT /api/v1/comments/:id/resolution`: right.** Body is exactly one boolean key, any query parameter or other body is refused before the engine is touched. The comment is read as the caller, so the object grant, the organization wall and the comment read gate (parent record readable) decide, and unreadable answers as unknown. A reply is refused. The one write is `is_resolved` by id; `resolved_by` and `resolved_at` come from the existing stamp hook and nothing else is in the payload. The body-edit stamp fires only on a changed `body`, so a resolve does not mark the comment edited. The answer carries the four resolution fields only. This is ruling 7063285032 inside the limits ruling 7069889899 set: no `sys_comment` update twin, comment text stays author-only.
- **`stampCommentResolution` reading `provenance.attributedUserId`: right.** The session user still wins; the attribution is read only when the write names no session user, and it is set server-side by the door, never by a client. No other writer in the plugin sets `is_resolved` true under an attributed system context (the reopen hook writes `false`, which clears the stamp), so no existing stamp changes.
- **Own-comment delete door, `DELETE /api/v1/comments/:id`: right.** It is the shared own-row kit unchanged in steps 1 to 6: read as the caller, then the structural `author_id` equals caller check, which is the only thing that admits the removal. `author_id` is platform-stamped and read-only, the right owner column. Another member's comment is refused even for a record editor, as ruled.
- **Kit step 7, `OwnRowDeleteDoor.refuseRemoval`: right, and it only narrows.** Optional, asked after the owner check and before the removal; the three existing doors declare none and are byte-for-byte the same path. The comment door's refusal (a reply exists under the comment) runs as a bare system read, which sees every reply regardless of the caller's read scope, so it errs toward refusing. Other rows keyed to a comment: reactions and attachments hold id columns with no delete behaviour, so the removal touches no other member's row; `parent_id` is the only lookup onto `sys_comment`.
- **Floor and grants: unchanged, confirmed in the diff.** `default-permission-sets.ts` is not in the file list: `owner_only_writes`, `sys_comment_moderation` and `member_default` are untouched, and so is the data door's resolve limb. The only `plugin-security` path is the new integration test, which pins the data door's 403s beside the doors' 200s on the shipped sets.
- **Caller resolution: right.** Both doors share the kit's one composition (session or API key, OAuth withheld, anonymous fail-closed, held sign-in refused). The resolution handler repeats the kit's steps 1 to 4 in the same order.
- **Public surface, each additive and optional: right.** `OwnRowDeleteDoor.refuseRemoval` (`@objectstack/core`); `DiscussionContextValue.ownCommentDeletesOnly` (`@object-ui/react`); `RecordCommentsData.ownDeletesOnly` and its key on `RecordCommentThreadProps['comments']` (`@object-ui/plugin-detail`); affordance row `feedCommentDeleteOwn` (`@object-ui/core`). `plugin-audit`'s index is not in the diff, so the door module's exports stay package-internal. Two ledger rows (`gap`, console is the consumer) with a conformance test; `check-route-envelope` declares the module.
- **Changed meaning of an existing prop: right, and not a narrowing.** The panel now draws the resolve control on every thread whenever the host passes `onResolveComment`, where it used to need `updatesOthersComments` for others' threads. Both the old meaning (#36104, #36178) and the new one are unreleased in the same release, the jsdoc states the host's new precondition, and the changeset carries the correction lines for both earlier notes.
- **Console: right.** Resolve always goes through the door; Delete goes through the data API with the delete grant and through the door without it, and `ownCommentDeletesOnly` keeps the offer to exactly what the door admits (own, no reply). A refused door call rejects and leaves the row.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `36186-36191-comment-doors.md`: `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/core`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/plugin-detail`, `@object-ui/react`, `@object-ui/core`. These are the six packages whose shipped source changes; `plugin-security` and `plugin-form` change tests only and are correctly absent.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and in the changeset, same sentence, and it names every surface the diff adds (two routes, the attribution read, `refuseRemoval`, the two optional UI members, the affordance row). Nothing is removed or re-typed, so no narrowing arm applies.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no `packages/spec` path, no schema, no stored-metadata shape. Under ruling A the level follows that line, and a Clause-② widening alone ships `patch`. Level stands.
- `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag, own comment with replies answers 409 (card #36191 item 2): answered, stands.** The card asked the PR to decide and state it; it does, in the maintainer summary and the changeset. It is the narrower of the available readings (the alternative clears `parent_id` on other members' replies through a system write), it follows ruling 7069889899's "not others'", and it is reversible by a later card. Administrators are unchanged.
- **Dev flag, external members who can read a thread may resolve it: answered, stands.** Ruling 7063285032 says anyone who can see the record. An external member reaches `sys_comment` only through an explicit grant and then passes the same read gates.
- **F1, should-fix, escalate to the maintainer, not blocking.** The door asks for a readable comment and no `sys_comment` write grant. Ruling 7063285032 reads "anyone who can see the record", and adds "the same gate as posting a comment". The two agree for every stock member, who holds comment create. They part for a principal that reads comments but holds no create on `sys_comment` (a deployment that grants a read-only set alone, or an external grant of read only): that principal cannot post, and can resolve through the door. The door follows the ruling's headline and the PR states "whoever can read the thread", so this is inside the ruling as written; the maintainer should confirm the headline is meant for a caller with no comment write grant, or the door should also ask the create grant. No test in the PR covers this principal either way.
- **F2, should-fix, not blocking.** The reply check and the removal are two statements with no shared transaction or re-check. A reply posted between them has its `parent_id` cleared by the system delete, which is the rewrite of another member's row that step 7 exists to prevent. The window is one request wide and the result is what an administrator's delete does today, so it does not widen who may delete what; it should be closed (one transaction, or a store-level refusal on the lookup for this path) or stated as a known limit.
- **F3, nit.** `feedCommentDeleteOwn` asks the `create` grant while the door asks none, so the console is narrower than the server for a read-only viewer who somehow authored a comment. Harmless, and consistent with `feedReactionRemove`.
- **SQL push-down: no finding.** The doors add a by-id `findOne` as the caller, a one-row `findOne` on `parent_id` as the existence probe, a by-id `update`, a by-id read-back and the kit's by-id `delete`. No id set is materialised and nothing is joined in the application. The panel's reply test reads rows it already holds.
- **Open questions: none left.** The PR files no follow-up; the "deleted comment placeholder" it mentions is a product question outside both cards.
- **Check-runs on the head: every run completed, none failed.** Green: Test Core and its 10 shards, Test UI and its 16 shards, TypeScript Type Check and the four Type Check lanes, Lint and Repo Gates and every Lint lane including Lint PM dispatch-gates, Build Core, Build Docs, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards. Skipped, as expected outside the merge queue or as opt-in: Queue verdict, Borrowed queue verdict, UI Published Artifacts, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, the Dogfood shard template row, Packed-tarball smoke, 18.x upgrade harness. No legacy commit status is reported.

No must-fix: neither door opens a field or a row beyond the rulings, and the floor and the moderation policy are unchanged.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1-c, delta) · repo:objectstack#1 · head `6069a983` · 2026-11-22T01:13Z

**Delta read:** `591de690..6069a983`, one commit, 12 files, +205 / −31. My ACCEPT 7071609534 stands for everything outside this delta.

**Gates:** CI is 63 success · 11 expected skip on `6069a983`, and mergeable is clean.

### F1: the posting gate (the resolution door's new step 6)
- **What it does.** After the as-caller read, and only if that read succeeds (so an unreadable comment is still the same 404 as an unknown id), the door asks the security service `canWriteObject('sys_comment', 'insert', context)`. Anything but `true`, or a throw, is 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, and nothing is written. The service is read per request (`getSecurity`), and a deployment with no security service admits, as posting does there.
